events.body_html: Well the invalid pointer error can't be from tempf; it must be from threadid[i]. And yes it would be OK to cast tempf back to FILE * and use it, provided you close it later with fclose().
What is an "invalid pointer error"? Please elaborate.

Just a shot in the dark but if you are passing in filenames on the command line then it looks like you are allocating 1 more thread and filename than you actually have because argc will be 1 larger because it counts argv[0] which is the program name.

Does this happen on your first join or your last one (i.e, what's i when you crash)? How does size relate to argc? Create a complete example that you can post (it won't be many more lines that you have above) that repros the problem with threads that do nothing at all but exit (and maybe display a message). You'll probably realize the problem as you're creating it...
Your comment on "invalid pointer" referrs to a line having pthread_create() but pthread_join(). Where does the actual error occurr? And is it a run-time or compile-time error?
I any case I'd strongly recommend to use error checking when doing system calls like malloc() et al and also the pthread_*() family of methods. This makes (debugging-)live much easier!
I'm voting to close this question as off-topic because OP needs to check the return value of pthread_create.
